utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, everybody. Before we start, are there any matters that the parties would like to bring to the attention of this Bench? Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have one matter, Your Honour. And it's related to the witness that we have an the stand at this point. Yesterday -- last -- yesterday evening, as I was going over and over the statement to prepare and reprepare for the case, I realised that when he was -- when the gentleman was questioned back on 30th June, 2002, they asked him -- they confronted him by -- that is, the OTP investigator, indicating that there was a person who would -- who had placed him at the Kravica warehouse during the period when the atrocities occurred, and it's on page 41, lines 6 through 9, of his statement. And -- in fact, I'll read it for the record. It says: "Apart from the footage and the photographic evidence that we have, we also have a person," a person, I underscore that, "who says you were at the warehouse during the execution phase. Can you comment on that." And Mr. Gajic says "I was not there." Later on as the interviews are about to end and I'm reading from page 44 and line 19 and onwards: "And I must tell you, the version that you have given us today does not completely match the version that we have already from other people," I underscore that, other people meaning plural, "and other information that we have. So before we take the interview back with us, are you sure there is nothing else that you've missed out that you haven't told us, because now is the time to tell us." Mr. Gajic says: "That's how it was. That's the essence." Based on that, it occurred to me that we need to -- I do not recollect coming across anyone mentioning Mr. Gajic's name. I have a Zylab programme, which has a search engine, and we have all the information from the OTP in there. We spent the better part of the night looking through that system trying to find any mentioning by of any witness. Mr. Gajic, during the interview, requested the name of the person and of course they didn't provide that information because it's a confidential informant, a protected witness. Needless to say, we did not come across any information of anyone or a person or people or other evidence that would suggest that Mr. Gajic was there. And so perhaps it was provided to us by the Prosecution and we don't have it or we haven't been able to locate it. If that is the case, I would like to know what it is, who is the person or persons and what other evidence they have. If they do not have that information, I would object to any line of questioning. Now, with [redacted], a similar question was posed by the Prosecution and said, "What if I were to tell you that there is a witness or people that place you at the Branjevo farm killing on the 16th of July, 1995." I did not object to that question because there was a good-faith basis for that question. I have that question and I do concur and I agree with their theory that that gentleman was most likely there during the executions, which is also referred to by one of their other witnesses, Mr. Erdemovic. So that's why I did not object. Here, however, unless there is a good-faith basis for that, I would object to any line of questioning. If there is a good-faith basis, I would ask that that be made on the record at this point. If they do have information, if they could provide it to us at this point. I apologise for bringing it up so late, but we spent a better part of the night looking for it and we didn't find it. I should also just add that when he was interviewed, Mr. Gajic indicated that he was with two other individuals, a Goran Djuric and a Dragan Bozic and in fact, it's also -- he repeated that in the proofing notes. We also did a computerised search for those names and we did not come across anything in our disclosure material that would give us the impression that they were -- that they were interviewed by the OTP. And Mr. Gajic indicated that when he went down to Kravica on that particular day, I believe it was the 13th, although he gets -- the dates may be wrong, he says the 14th. He says he was there for half an hour with these two gentlemen, so one would expect that if he was a suspect when he was interviewed, they would double-check it. We don't have that information. So I don't know where they got this information, but I would ask that a good-faith basis be made at this time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I believe that you have to understand that the testimony of a live witness sometimes has some discrepancies with any statements or interviews conducted before. We believe that we could see how this witness will answer the questions posed by the Prosecutor. Are there any response from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, Mr. Karnavas said a lot. I don't fully understand everything he was saying, but I do think that much of this we can work out privately. A lot of it sounded like discovery issues, things like that. I can say that I believe the people that the questioner was referring to were the victims of the Kravica warehouse that said there was a lot of killing going on. And as you'll hear, this witness said he didn't see any of that. I think that's pretty clear. And on the other matter, I will speak to Mr. Karnavas about. We'll research the issues and see what the situation is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think at this stage we'll allow the Prosecution to put any questions concerning of the incident in that warehouse. But at the same time, the Defence counsel has the full right to cross-examine this witness thoroughly. Bear in mind that there are always some discrepancies between the live testimony and the previous statement and the conversations. That's why we only admitted the live testimony into the evidence, other than any previous statement and conversations unless there is extraordinary circumstances. Mr. Karnavas, could we proceed on this line?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and I agree with you totally that there are always discrepancies. I just want to be abundantly clear, because maybe I wasn't. They suggested, the OTP, Mr. Bursik in fact, said that there was a person that places him. Now, I understand there are witnesses that say they saw Serb soldiers, but if they're going to point the finger at this person who is a member of the Bratunac Brigade, there should at least be a good-faith basis, otherwise it's a fishing expedition. And of course, I understand we're dealing with professional Judges, and there will be no weight to the question being posed unless there is a good-faith basis to substantiate that. Nonetheless, I'm just bringing it to the Court's attention, because I did a search and I don't have anything and I was wondering if they have and if so I missed it and I needed to know and I'm just doing my job.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe it all depends on how the witness will answer the question posed by the Prosecution during the following proceedings. Maybe this question is touched upon, maybe it is not. I hope that during the breaks the parties could meet together and solve these things out, other than we have a long debate in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your cooperation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Did you have a good rest last night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite a good rest, yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So you're ready to continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Davis.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic, you told us when we left off yesterday you had told us that your section of the line of defence had moved south towards the village of Cizmici. Let me ask you, were you aware when you were with your platoon reinforcing the line of defence that Srebrenica had fallen?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we didn't know for certain, but we did assume that Srebrenica had fallen. We heard that.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: And when did you learn for certain that Srebrenica had fallen?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly, but as soon as the UN checkpoint -- as the UN withdrew from the checkpoint, the assumption was that Srebrenica had fallen.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you confirmed with anyone that Srebrenica had, in fact, fallen?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing specific.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: I would like to ask the usher to place P162, the map we were looking at yesterday, on the ELMO again.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: And if you wouldn't mind, Mr. Gajic, if you could point out on the map the location of your battalion command.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was about here.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Do you recall marking the map with the location of the Italian command in our offices on Monday?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: And can you tell the Judges what letter you assigned the location of the battalion command.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The letter B.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: How far is that command headquarters from the Konjevic Polje/Bratunac road?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps between 500 metres and 1 kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: In these days after the fall of Srebrenica, when was the first time that you returned to Magasici, to the battalion command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could have -- if the question could be rephrased, returned, returned from where?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if you may.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic, you've told us that you were on the line of defence in the area of Cizmici in the days following the fall of Srebrenica. From that time, when was the first time that you then returned to the battalion command at Magasici?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps a day or two later, after we had moved.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: And tell me what happened after you arrived at the battalion command.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the people there had already found out that Srebrenica had fallen and we heard that there were many captured people.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: What did you hear about the captured people?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We heard that they had been put up in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Did you hear where in Kravica that they had been put in up?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The warehouse, the warehouse belonging to an agricultural institution.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: When you said there were many captured people, to whom are you referring?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Who did you see when you were at the battalion command?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were soldiers there, our soldiers. We who were there throughout this period.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: When you say "our soldiers," were there soldiers from other units within the Kravica Battalion?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Were there members of your platoon there at the battalion command?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some. We were together.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: And were there officers there at the battalion command?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one in particular. All the people who had been there before.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: And who were they?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't say exactly, but I would assume the battalion commander Vidovic, his deputies, those people.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: When you -- how long did you stay at the command?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. Not long, though.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Can you give me an estimate? Was it a matter of hours?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps, yes. An hour or two.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: And when you left the command, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To Kravica, Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Why did you go to Kravica?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Out of sheer curiosity, because we heard what had happened and we just walked over there to see if there was anyone there that we knew.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Did you go alone?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went with two other colleagues of mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Who went with you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The battalion driver and another man, another soldier, a friend.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: If you could refer again to P162, the map next to you, and indicate the location of Kravica and the letter with which you marked Kravica when you were in my offices on Monday.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kravica is where the letter D stands.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: And approximately how far from the command battalion -- battalion command at Magasici is Kravica?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 5 or 6 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Do you recall what time you arrived in the village of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but it was in the afternoon. Perhaps at 3.00 or 4.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: And how did you get there?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By car. We drove there.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: What route did you take?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We took the Bratunac/Konjevic Polje road.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: What did you see along the Bratunac/Konjevic Polje road as you were driving to Kravica?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing special.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Were there soldiers along the road?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Were there vehicles along the road?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We may have driven past someone, but aside from that there was nothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Were there any groups of Muslim prisoners that you saw along the road?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We didn't see anyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: When you arrived in Kravica, what did you find?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We saw groups of Muslims at the warehouse, the warehouse belonging to the agricultural company.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Were they -- when you say "groups of Muslims," were there more than one group?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all there in the same place, at least those that I saw.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Who else was in the area there in Kravica, near the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't quite understand. Who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Was there anybody at Kravica, other than a group of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, our soldiers were there.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: How many soldiers did you see there?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. It was a small group.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: And how were these soldiers dressed?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing special. They wore whatever they had to wear. Some had regular olive-drab, some had regular camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Were there any soldiers with headgear, headwear?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, but I don't think I noticed any wearing any headgear.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Did you recognise the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Were the soldiers armed?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly. Everyone was armed back then.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: What sorts of weapons did you notice on the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Did you talk to the soldiers or ask them what was going on there?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: You mentioned that there were "our soldiers there," when you said "our soldiers," what did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serbian soldiers, the soldiers of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: And roughly how many soldiers did you see at Kravica?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps a rather small platoon or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: How many would that be in a platoon?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but maybe between 15 and 20 men, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: I'd like to refer you now to an exhibit that has previously been admitted as P10.1. I am going to ask the usher to put it on the ELMO and it will also appear on the monitors. Mr. Gajic, do you recognise what's depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: And what is it?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the agricultural organisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Is this the warehouse to which you've been referring?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: And can you point -- because there's a number of buildings on the photograph, can you point to the building that you recognise as the warehouse using the pointer there.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one here.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived at the warehouse, from which direction were you coming in the car?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the direction of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: And you say that you saw a group of Muslims. Can you, using the pen, mark with a number 1 where you saw the group of Muslims.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: And how many Muslims were in this group of Muslims that you saw?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I don't know the exact number. This part here -- I don't know exactly how many.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: When you say "this part here," what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in this part here, halfway up to this wall, but I don't know exactly how many there were.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: You -- I asked you to mark with a 1 where you saw the Muslim men. Is that the location where you were standing when you saw them or where the Muslims were?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an open area here, so I was somewhere about here. I don't know whether it was 1 metre in front or behind, but I was in this part and I could see from there.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: And you indicated the left side of the building was where the Muslim men were positioned. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Were they sitting or standing?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were sitting.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: And was the area full that you've indicated on the left-hand side of the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Would you approximate, were there more than 100 men there?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I don't know the size of that area so that I could work it out, but let's say there were about 100.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: How were the Muslims dressed?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends. Some were wearing civilian clothes, some in uniforms, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: And the men that you saw in the warehouse, were they alive?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Are you aware that a number of prisoners were killed at Kravica warehouse on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: And what did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that some people were killed there.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: From whom did you hear about this?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly from the soldiers. Stories were going around, so that's how I heard of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Do you recall when you heard about the killings at Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps a day afterwards or in the evening, something like that, when I returned to Magasici again.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Now, while you were at Kravica, were there any vehicles in the area?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this part where I was, there weren't any. But before the warehouse, I could see that there were some on the road; I saw that on my way back.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: How far from the warehouse on the road were the vehicles?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 500 metres, perhaps, a kilometre, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Were they parked or were they moving?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some were parked and some were just driving along slowly.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: What types of vehicles were they?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly trucks and buses.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: And did you notice whether there were people in the vehicles, aside from the driver?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I noticed, yes. There were people.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Do you know who was in the vehicles?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know personally, but I can assume.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: What do you assume?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that they were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Turning back to the exhibit, the paragraph that's on the ELMO, you mentioned that you saw some soldiers while you were at Kravica, where were the soldiers that you saw?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly along the road and in this area here.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Can you please mark with a number 2 where you saw the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's right here.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: During the period that you were at Kravica, did you see any photographers or film crews there?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did notice cameramen.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: And where did you see the cameramen?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the Konjevic Polje/Bratunac road in front of the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: When you were interviewed by the OTP in June 2003, were you under the impression that you had been photographed at Kravica?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: How long were you at the warehouse in Kravica on that day?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 5, 6 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Were any additional prisoners brought to the warehouse while you were there?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't notice anything during the time that I was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Were any prisoners shot while you were there?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: When you left the warehouse, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To Magasici.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: When you say --

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the command.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: And what route did you take?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same road, just going in the direction of Bratunac. So Bratunac, Konjevic Polje, and then we went back.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: When you arrived back at the command, did you talk to anyone there about what you saw -- had seen at Kravica, I should say?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, mostly to the soldiers. Of course, we soldiers talked amongst ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Did you speak to your commander about what you had seen?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Was he there when you arrived at the battalion command?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't know. We didn't really have any special contacts, not even before that.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: And how long did you stay at the command?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly. Perhaps I went back to the front lines that same evening or the next morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: And how long were you on the front lines after that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps for another two or three days.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly nothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: What do you mean "mostly nothing"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it's self explanatory. Mostly nothing means mostly nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we cannot be assisted by this question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe, Ms. Davis, you could be more specific. What happened is very broad.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: When you returned to the front lines, was there any combat activity that your platoon was involved in?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Did you capture any prisoners?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't, not anybody.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: What were your duties while you were on the defence line after you returned from the battalion command?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing in particular. We formed the line in the event of any attacks, but specifically nothing happened. We were just fooling around, sleeping, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: And how many -- for how many days did you remain there on the front lines?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that already, perhaps for another two or three days.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: And then where did you go after that?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Back to Magasici again and then after that to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: And how long were you in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but perhaps for two or three days.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Were these days off that you had?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, mostly I was off.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Did you ever return to the front lines after your days off?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Did you have permission to go to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't ask anyone for permission.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: And how long did you stay in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About a month.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Did you ever return to your platoon?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any cross-examination, Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand that you were with the Bratunac Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The 1st Battalion?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The intervention unit?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you had -- you're from that area, in fact, the Kravica area, that's where you were born and raised?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And of course because of the war situation, you were expected to serve in that particular area. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And as I understand it from 1992 -- well, before 1992 you had already served, you had done your national service with the JNA. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then when the war came, you began your service sometime around 1992 all the way until after the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And during that entire time that you were serving with the Bratunac Brigade, you were located more or less in the same area?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that was a defensive line?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And of course part of the reason for that being a defensive line was because on the other side of the line there were Muslim soldiers primarily in the Srebrenica area. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And of course, with the fall of Srebrenica there was no need for you, I suspect, for you to be there any longer?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I would suspect that might be the reason why after you -- the fall of Srebrenica and after going to Serbia, you didn't return to your battalion. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, on the -- before we get to the events, I want to talk to you a little bit about your interview. Do you recall you were interviewed back on June 30th, 2002. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And during that period you were asked certain questions about the events?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you were asked particular questions with respect to you being in Kravica sometime on the 13th or the 14th of July. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And when you were asked those questions, you gave the best answers or the answers that you thought were truthful and honest. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: For instance, you were asked with whom you had gone there. And you were able to remember one name, I believe that was Goran Djuric, right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But you also indicated that you had -- that there was another man present with you, but you did not recall his name. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But you had indicated that you knew that while you were there you had been filmed, videotaped?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, you requested to see the footage of the video so you could assist the investigator of the OTP in order to give the name of the individual with whom you were?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And initially, Investigator Bursik of the Office of the Prosecution indicated to your request, and I quote on page 18 of your statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And for the record it's D65/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in your page it would be page 21, lines 1 to 23. You state: "One was Goran Djuric. He was the driver in the battalion. I don't remember the name of the second person. I'm not sure who that was. If you have any footage to show me, then I would probably remember the person or at least show you who that was." And Mr. Bursik answered: "I've got some footage, but we'll get to that later if you can continue with the story." Do you recall Mr. Bursik telling you that he had the footage and that you and he would get to it later on?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: There's an objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Davis.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Sorry. I believe Mr. Karnavas said that Mr. Bursik -- read correctly from the transcript that Mr. Bursik said he had "some" footage and in Mr. Karnavas's question he suggests that he told him he had "the" footage. I just want to be clear that Mr. Bursik did indicate only that he had "some" footage of Kravica warehouse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: For the record let me read it again because it's a critical point and thank my colleague for pointing that out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Getting back to page 18, stay with me, sir, Mr. Bursik says: "I've got some footage but we'll get to that later." Do you recall Mr. Bursik saying that, "we will get to that later"?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I gather that when he told you he would get to the footage later with you, you expected that he would show you some footage. Right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Now, let's go to page 42. And in your page it would be page 50. And I'll read a little bit. And I will start from line 20 on page 42 at the bottom, you indicate, somewhere on page 50, sir, you indicate to a question: "I don't know because I think the photograph of the shots were taken from the vehicle." You're being asked about a person taking the video. Mr. Bursik, that is on page 43, line 1: "Okay. Did this vehicle pass or did it stop and so that people got out" -- line 16, sir. Your answer: "I think that the vehicle just passed by."

utterances.speaker: MR. BURSIK
utterances.text: "Okay. I'm going to give you the opportunity now to clarify anything that we have said in this interview which you feel that you have not properly been able to express yourself." You state: "If you have that footage or a photograph or whatever of the place, because I would like to see it as I am not sure who the third person was." Mr. Bursik of the Office of the Prosecution: "We are not going to show you that footage now because the other that -- there's two other teams with the interviews so they have all the footage with them at the moment." Your answer: "Nema problema, not a problem." Then Mr. Bursik: "Also, it's not really going to serve too much purpose to show you the same footage, I mean, you were there already." You respond: "The reason I'm asking that is I'm not sure about the people that were with me. I'm sure about Djuric, but I'm not sure about the third one and that's why I'm not sure." And Mr. Bursik says: "Okay." Do you recall that exchange, sir?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you get the impression after that that there was no inclination on the part of the Office of the Prosecution or this particular investigator to ever show you the footage so that you could identify the person you were with just in case they may wish to contact them to verify what you had told them?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically just that investigator, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, during that investigation, sir, is it not a fact that they had indicated to you that there was a person who had seen you there during the time when executions were taking place?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I was told.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: I'm not sure that's what it states.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm just doing the general. I'm going to get to the specific.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Davis.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: I believe it's just a question of wording. He indicated someone had seem him there during the executions. I think someone placed him there but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Davis. Let's come to that specific paragraph first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Page 41 of the transcript, I must apologise, sir, I don't have the number. If I can just read it and then we'll try to find the page in Srpski. "Apart from the footage and the photographic evidence that we have, we have a person who says you were at the warehouse during the execution phase. Can you comment on that?" It's on page 48, sir, line 14. That's where I'm reading, and I apologise for not being more prepared, Your Honours. "Apart from the footage and the photographic evidence that we have, we also have a person who says that you were at the warehouse during the execution phase. Can you comment on that?" And your answer was: "I was not there."

utterances.speaker: MR. BURSIK
utterances.text: "Why would someone falsely implicate you?" Your answer: "I would like to see that person. If that person could confirm that in front of me because I was not there."

utterances.speaker: MR. BURSIK
utterances.text: "Unfortunately he's a protected witness. I just wanted to let you know that is why we are treating you as a suspect today." And your answer, or your response: "I was not there. I did not fire a single shot in that area." Do you recall that exchange, sir?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: They never gave you the name of the person, did they?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: They never gave you any other information that would at least give some confirmation that you were there?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: They just accused you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I want to talk a little bit about you being there. First, serving in the 1st Battalion, there were several commanders that were above you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The commander of the 1st Battalion was Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then there was a deputy commander, I believe his name was Vasic, Lazo Vasic, I might get the pronunciation wrong.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Then I believe in your platoon there was a platoon commander by the name of, I'll skip his first name, Djukanovic is his last name. Right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it Mr. Djukanovic was your immediate commander, since you were in that platoon, he was your immediate commander. Right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, on the 13th of July, you had heard that there was some people in the warehouse in the area in which you had grown up in. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that one of the reasons you and your friends went there was because you were curious to see who was there and whether you would recognise anyone?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Out of sheer curiosity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You had been on the line for quite a long time. The imminent threat was no longer there, and out of curiosity you decided to take a drive down there. Right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a fair assessment, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: As I understand it, when you were interviewed by the Office of the Prosecution, you informed them that you were there 15 to 20 minutes sometime between the hours of 3.00 or 4.00, although you're not sure?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe that's the total amount of time that I was there, but I spent less time near the warehouse. But, yes, that all was happening at about 3.00 or 4.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So you took a look, you saw what was happening, you didn't see anyone that you recognised, and then you left?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And of course before going there, before going there, you did not ask permission to leave the area in which you were stationed. Right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I didn't ask any kind of permission. That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it nobody or your platoon commander did not notice your absence during the period that it took for you to drive there, take a look, and drive back. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even if he'd noticed, it wouldn't have meant anything. It was just time off that we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But fair to say, it's fair to say that you went there without permission? You were on your own for that period of time?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a fair statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And we certainly can't -- we certainly can say that you were not ordered to go there. That we can say for certain, right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you were not sent there on some reconnaissance mission to find out what was happening?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, by no means. It was just for curiosity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's move back a little bit. We talked about you being on this line from 1992 to 1995, that line of defence. Sir, during the attack on Srebrenica, did you and your platoon advance at all between, say, the 6th and the 10th -- 11th of July. Did your line advance toward Srebrenica to try to capture Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, at some time, either during the late evening of the 10th, sometime in the 11th, you and members of your platoon, most likely members of your battalion, noticed a large movement of Muslims leaving the Srebrenica area. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And they were heading towards Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the general direction, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In the general direction. And we could safely say that from Zvornik they would probably be heading towards Tuzla, because that was the route that one would take in that area. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume so. Tuzla was their final destination, but I don't know, but it was their territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And from where you were, they were approximately 2 or 3 kilometres away?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you could say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you could see this large group of people passing through?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, on accountant of the lay of the land as I say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the lay of the land is more like no man's land; in other words, nobody's sitting there guarding that line. It's in between lines, is it not?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. No one was covering that area, none of our soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But at some point, your commander, Mr. Ostojic asked you to strengthen the line, is that correct, strengthen the line where you were situated?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the reason for that was, and correct me if I'm wrong, in the eventuality that that large group of Muslims came towards your location. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. That's the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And none came?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you didn't advance forward?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You weren't asked, say, like the allied forces or the American soldiers in Afghanistan or Iraq to hunt down or chase and kill that group of people that were walking or passing through that area, were you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we were not. None of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, in fact, -- and in fact, they all went through and not a single shot was fired at that large group of people from your platoon. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly not by our platoon or battalion. That space was left for them to pass through.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you never received any orders to advance toward that group of people that were walking by in order to capture or to ambush or to kill. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We never received any order like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic, your cross-examination, if you have.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have no questions for this witness. This witness has nothing to do with the defence of my client. Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any re-direct, Ms. Davis?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Very briefly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic, you did, in fact, advance on the UN checkpoint, isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did say that yesterday, but it was a day or two after that. We had moved as far as the village of Cizmici.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: And your portion of the line in fact moved south in the direction of Srebrenica toward the UN checkpoint. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Judge Vassylenko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic, you said that you went to Kravica out of curiosity. My question: What caused your curiosity?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had been born in the area, you know, born and bred. There were Muslims there who were my schoolmates, and that was the sole reason for my curiosity. I might as well have seen someone I knew.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: But your schoolmates were in Kravica before, yes, but why at that very moment you remembered that your schoolmates were in Kravica and decided to go to Kravica.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure what you mean when you say "before."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Well, your schoolmates lived in Kravica, yes, before --

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: -- before Srebrenica had fallen and why did you go to see Kravica just when Srebrenica was fallen?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we heard that there were many Muslims there who had surrendered. That was the only reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And when Muslims were surrendered, then what? You just wanted to go to Kravica to see surrendered Muslims?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. The story was -- the story started circulating that there were people there who had surrendered and we just wanted to go there to see if there were any people that we knew among those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any questions out of Judges questions? Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour. Just to clarify a point that Judge Vassylenko was asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Prior to the war there were Muslims residing there, were there not?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Near Kravica in the area, yes. I'm not sure what belongs to the Kravica area. You mean the local commune of Kravica, yes, there were Muslims living there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you had friends that were living there?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it during the war, they left and went to other areas, one of them being Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, during those days, you had also heard that a friend of yours who was a Muslim was at the health centre who was a soldier. Is that correct? Abid Sinanovic.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Abid Sinanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And isn't it a fact that you went to the health centre to see him and also to give him cigarettes?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked questions about where I was and I, on the other hand, heard that he was there, so I went there to see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you offered him some cigarettes, right? You talked?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We talked briefly, and yes, I gave him cigarettes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you told this to the Prosecution, to the Office of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Ms. Davis.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: I don't have any further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. At this stage are there any documents to tender? Ms. Davis?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have two exhibits that we would like to tender. P162, which is the map of the northern portion of the Srebrenica enclave that was marked by the witness in our offices that he's been referring to during his testimony. The second is now numbered as P163. This is the aerial of Kravica warehouse that was marked by the witness that was previously admitted unmarked as P10.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. These two documents are admitted into the evidence. Are there any documents on the Defence part?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have nothing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague for giving your evidence. The usher will show you out of the room and we wish you a pleasant journey back home. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, as for the next witness, could somebody brief us about any protective machines.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, Your Honour, the next witness we would like a pseudonym as well as face distortion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I think we should set up some preparations during the break. Now we'll break and we'll resume at 10 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper the usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much, you may sit down, please. Before we start, I have to tell you that you may object to making any statement that might intend to incriminate yourself. But however, the Chamber could compel you to answer the question. The testimony compelled in this way should not be used as evidence in a subsequent prosecution against you for any offense, other than the false testimony. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, very much. Ms. Issa, are you ready to proceed?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. I'm just going to start off, sir, by asking you what your ethnic background or nationality is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I'm a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what is your educational background?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I have completed secondary education and I am a trained worker with construction equipment.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And during the war, sir, through July of 1995, where did you work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: During the war, I worked with water plumbing, repairing the water lines and the asanacija of the terrain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, you have to bear in mind that this witness is a protected witness. If you want to ask some background questions, we might go to private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour, and I was going to get to that at some point. I think at this point it may not be a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And perhaps out of an abundance of caution, we may just start going to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in open session. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you tell us what your tasks were, sir, during the period of July 1995.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: When I left the line or before?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: When you left the line.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: -- What my tasks were. Okay, thank you. When I came down from the Obli Vis line, I reported to the command of the communal utilities company. I found Dragan Mirkovic there and he told me that there were a lot of dead from the fighting between the two armies, that the next day they were to be buried at our Serbian cemetery, the Serbian soldiers and the civilians. And then when I finished that, there were orders that followed from the same person, from this Dragan Mirkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do you recall, sir, the date or when you were given the orders to bury the dead, the Serbian nationals that you referred to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: This could have been on the 12th or the 13th of July in the evening, after the fall of Srebrenica. Those boys -- those men, those soldiers, had to be buried.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And do you remember how long it took you to complete that task?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: At least a day or two was needed to complete all of these burials of Serbian soldiers at our cemetery, and that is something that nobody asks any questions about.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And after you completed your work at the cemetery burying the Serb nationals, what was the next order that you were given?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: The next order was to then proceed with the burial of the dead Muslims who were killed in the combat in Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And when did you receive this order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I received this order after the burial of the Serbian soldiers at the cemetery, so it would be on the second or the third day.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And who gave you the order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Dragan Mirkovic issued the order and took me in front of the command where there was a kind of wooden shack where the military police was, and that's where Momir Nikolic confirmed this order.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And do you recall, sir, what Momir Nikolic said to you when he confirmed the order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: There wasn't really too much talk. This job had to be done. It had to be completed because disease was spreading in the area around Bratunac. There was combat going on, and disease was spreading. There was a lot to be done and it had to be done.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, before I ask you the next question, sir, I'm just going to ask you to put aside your transcript for the moment and we'll refer to it as needed if you need to refresh your memory. Just leave it there, that's fine. Okay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I don't need it. Everything is written up here in my head.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Was there anybody else with Dragan Mirkovic and Momir Nikolic at the time that you had this conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: There was nobody there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps, sir, to assist you in refreshing your memory, I would ask you to refer to page 18, line 7, of your transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And in the English version, Your Honour, it's page 30, lines 1 to 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Have you read that to yourself, sir? Do you now recall as to whether or not there was anyone else with Dragan Mirkovic and Momir Nikolic when you had this conversation or you were given the order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: It states there Nikolic and then in front of that it says Jole. Jole was in Kravica when they were loading at the agricultural cooperative. He was the director of that company.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And was he there initially before you went to Kravica? Was he there, just to clarify, when you received the initial order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: It states there that he was, so it's possible that he was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But you don't recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I don't recall that. There are many similar answers here in these papers, so yesterday when I was reading that over, there are a lot of repeated or double responses.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. That's fine, sir. You can now put that away for the time being. Could you describe the location, sir, when you met with Mr. Momir Nikolic and Dragan Mirkovic and you had the conversation or you were given the order.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: You are persistent with this. I told you, in front of the wooden shack which was there, that's where the military police was. And this is where I met them and that's where they issued the order to me. I've already said that once.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. What happened, what did you do after you were given this order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Just like any soldier, I had to receive this order, accept this order, and I set out to implement the task.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I went in the direction of Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And how did you know to go there or to go to that specific location of Glogova?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Because that's what they said, to go to Glogova, and they went in their car, they went in front. And I was driving slowly in my machine behind them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And around -- do you recall around what time you reached Glogova?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Perhaps an hour or an hour and 15 minutes after them, so it was around 8.00, because the order was received in the morning, so we set out in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what happened when you reached your location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I arrived there. They were already there and they showed me where the grave was to be dug, in which direction. It was a large mass grave about 10, 15, or 20 metres long and about 2 metres wide.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And can you describe the location, sir, where it was to be dug.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can describe it. It was parallel with the road. It was a village path road towards Glogova and Konjevic Polje. Investigators were already there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And you said, sir, that they showed you the location. Can you tell us who were they.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: When I say "they," I mean Dragan Mirkovic, my superior, and Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Right, sir, referring then to Prosecutor Exhibit P164. I'm just going to ask that that be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can just have the Court's indulgence for a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, you see that diagram, sir, that's been placed on the machine next to you. Can you tell us first of all, sir, where this diagram came from.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I made the diagram when the investigators in Banja Luka asked me about this. This is a diagram that I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And can you tell us, sir, what the diagram depicts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: The diagram depicts the place where pits one and two were dug in order to bury the Muslim soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we're going to get to pit number two, but for the time being can you point to the first grave that you dug or the location that you were shown and that you ultimately dug.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you take the pointer and point to that, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just for the record, Your Honour, he is pointing to a location that is on the left-hand side from the direction of Bratunac and Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, at this stage, I want to ask for some clarifications. The document is the P164 and we are provided with another document P161 with the name of this witness. Are they the same document?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: They are, Your Honour. What we've done was we simply folded that part over such so that the name of the witness would not appear on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this clarification.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, sir. Now, after you were shown the location of this grave by Dragan Mirkovic and Momir Nikolic, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: They told me what to do, so I started to work. I started to dig the graves. I was digging for a long time. I was digging practically for the whole day. Trucks were bringing in bodies for burial.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And we'll get to that, but can you first tell us how large was the grave that you dug?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: As I said a moment ago, between 10, 15, maybe 20 metres in length, 2 metres across. It was a metre and a half deep at most.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And why did you dig those particular dimensions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Because the lorry had to enter some way down the pit and tip the bodies inside.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And did anybody instruct you to dig the grave in any particular manner or give you the particular dimensions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: No, no one. They said generally dig in that direction. I have dug 20 such Serb graves, identical ones.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Perhaps, sir, to assist you in refreshing your memory, I would like you to refer to page 26, line 21 through 31 of your transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And in the English version, Your Honour, it's page 44, line 16 through 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The page and the line that is reflecting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think you have to speak directly into your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I apologise. The page and the line that I have doesn't seem to comport with what is being asked. I wonder if the pagination is correct or is there another version that...

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I believe there was a revised version that was disclosed to Defence counsel last week, I think Thursday. It does not substantially change anything from the first version. There may be a couple of words added here and there and that may have affected the pagination. I'm referring to the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm looking at the revised version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is that the correct page. Maybe you could repeat the page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm looking at the original version, Your Honour. It's page 44, line 16 through 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll plug along, Your Honour, but I assume that since we had a revised version we would be going through the revised version and my old version doesn't have any lines, but I'll manage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Does that, sir, assist you in refreshing your memory whether or not you received instructions as to the particular dimensions of the grave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Well, it's the same thing that I said. It wasn't specified, they just told us about the area, how big an area, I said about 20 metres, 2 metres across. That's exactly what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And what happened, sir, after you started to dig the grave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I dug -- I kept digging for about four or five hours without completing my work. The lorries kept bringing in bodies, bodies of men who had been killed in battle. I moved aside for the lorries to tip the bodies into the pit.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And before we get to the lorries, sir, can you describe the type of machine you were using when you were digging the grave.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: That time, I was using a tipper owned by the Bratunac public utilities company. And the tipper is still being -- the tipper truck is still being used. It's still in use. It's not very often that it's actually in good working order, but it's still being used for repairing the water lines and also for digging graves.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this looks like, what does the machine look like.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I can. This machine has a claw in front that can -- that has the capacity for a certain amount of material, and in the back it has another arm that's about 4 metres long, which is at the back of this machine. That's also used for a number of different operations.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Issa, I think we have been provided with a kind of graphic pictures on those machines. I don't know whether you have it at your hands. Maybe you could provide it to the witness and ask him to identify what kind of machine he was using at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, we -- I'll be able to do that, I suppose, momentarily. I'm just going to obtain those photographs momentarily. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Was anybody present, sir, while you were digging the grave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: No, not at that time. I was the only one doing that. Who would have wanted to be there with that smell of decomposing bodies, to stand by, to watch, to breathe the air? I was actually wearing a mask as I was doing this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. You indicated earlier, sir, that there were lorries coming and bringing the dead bodies at the time while you were digging the graves. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes. Every now and then the lorries would arrive to tip the bodies into the grave.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And how many lorries or trucks do you recall being there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: There were two yellow lorries and two red ones. One of the red ones was often out of order and it wasn't being used that much.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know -- starting then with the two yellow lorries, do you know which -- where these lorries came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: What do you mean where they came from? Who they belonged to; is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, who they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
