utterances.text: One of the yellow lorries belonged to the same unit of the public utilities company that I was in. It was used to clean the streets of the town. That's what I was used for. And the other one was owned by the brick factory in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what about the two red ones?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: The two red ones were property of the Sasa [phoen] mines, which I believe also belongs to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And can you tell us, sir, who were the drivers of these -- of the lorries, starting with the yellow truck from the public utilities company.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes. The public utilities lorry was driven by a colleague of mine named Cvjetinovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you know do you know what his first name is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm willing to be somewhat flexible in these instances, so I don't object to counsel giving him the name and saying would this be correct? I think it would move the process along somewhat, but only in these limited instances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you for your cooperation and the suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm just not sure if there was an objection there, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, no, it's not an objection. It's trying to help you with this situation. You may say the name to this witness and ask him whether this was the person.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And for the record, Your Honour, I'm referring to page 52, line 13 of the original version. And while the witness is doing that, Your Honour, I just want to indicate that I do believe that a letter was sent to counsel indicating that I will be referring to the original version of the transcript. So he was advised of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the original version does not have lines. Also, we were just informed that when they did the transcript back in -- when this man was interviewed back on 29 June, 2003, it was just revealed to us a couple of days ago that apparently part of the interview was not even tape recorded because they had double taped on one of the tapes of the interview. This is new information to us. Now, if they want to provide us with an old version with lines, I can follow along, but the one I have received from the OTP does not have lines, the new one does. Nonetheless, I've indicated that I'm willing to work with counsel to manage to find the appropriate sections. They seem to be approximately half a page down the road. Once she begins reading, I can find it. So there's no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe you could count these lines by yourself.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall, sir, what time the trucks arrived that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: They kept arriving for a time in the afternoon one after the other. I can't give you the precise period of time, but it was in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what happened when the trucks arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Once the trucks had arrived, I moved my equipment to the side so they could get down into the pit and tip the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Could you estimate the number of bodies that were placed into the pit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I can't give you the exact number of bodies, but say, for example, you could fit between 15 and 20 bodies into the yellow trucks, and they did two or three rounds each. So you can multiply that and see what the result is. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what about the red trucks, how many bodies could you fit in those trucks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: The red ones were somewhat larger than the yellow ones, about 15 bodies, but probably even more, more bodies than the yellow ones.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you recall how many times they returned with bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: As I said a minute ago, they did two or three rounds on that day and the following day, too; one round each.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did the bodies fill the capacity of the grave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Perhaps they did fill the capacity, perhaps not, but I would turn those bodies gradually.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: What do you mean you would turn those bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I was covering them up with earth, forming a layer of earth on top, and then I would put the finishing touch to the grave the next day with another layer of earth.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you speak with the drivers at the time that the bodies were being placed into the pit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I wish you were there to try take off your mask and breathe the air that was there. Of course I couldn't speak to the driver. You couldn't even keep your eyes open, let alone speak to anyone. The horrible stench of decomposing bodies that was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir, just so you understand, I have to ask you these questions so the Court can understand what happened. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I understand all of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. What was the condition of the bodies when you -- when they were thrown into the pit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: The bodies had been in that shape for about three or four days decomposing and infection was spreading and you had to bury them as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you recall what the -- what clothing were on the bodies? Can you describe the clothing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: There were military uniforms there. The bodies were spattered with blood and there were civilian clothes on some of the bodies, too, because the soldiers would change their clothing in the woods and dump civilian clothes, as opposed to military uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Is that what you said when you were asked this question by the investigators in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Maybe not in these same words, but I did say that the bodies were spattered with blood and some of the bodies at uniforms on and some of the bodies had civilian clothes on. I'm sure that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: What happened after the grave was filled with bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Once the grave was filled with bodies, I kept working laying on the second layer of earth over those bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And when did you complete covering up the grave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I don't think I was able to complete that day. I kept working the next day, but I believe I've already said this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And what did you do at the end of that day before you returned the next day to cover up the graves?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And who is this man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: This man was a military policeman. We didn't know him. In the evening, I think it was about 10.00 in the evening, he came in a black uniform and he had what I believed was a Sarajevo accent, but that's all I knew. He threatened us, told us that we had to go. We weren't brave enough to go because it was night and the front lines were near, so we only set out the next morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell us, sir, what he was referring to, you had to go where and do what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes, he threatened us and told us that we should go to Kravica and load there the bodies from the agricultural cooperative, the bodies that were there, those, too, he said should be buried in the grave. We tried to defend ourselves by saying that we had no fuel to go there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And did that work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: It didn't work. The lorry with fuel arrived and after about half an hour of us trying to convince him, we had to go. We went ahead, a kilometre perhaps, but then we took shelter, because we weren't brave enough to proceed in the dark.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Well, just to be clear, sir, to clarify, did you go to Kravica that evening or the next morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: The next morning at dawn we set out with our machines. It would have taken us at least one and a half hours, up to two hours, to reach Kravica. As soon as dawn cracked, we set out, and the machines were parked near our houses by the roadside.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know to what brigade or unit or part of the army that this military policeman was attached to?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's been asked and answered, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's been asked and answered. He indicated that he thought he was a police officer, he was dressed in black, and he has a Sarajevo accent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But that particular question was not asked. You may proceed, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you answer that question, sir? Do you know what army or unit -- what part of the army or brigade he was attached to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I object. It's leading in nature now. What army. It could have been that he was with MUP, dressed in black carrying weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I understand, I understand. Well, we'd better use the neutral words, maybe unit or something like this, not army or troop or soldier.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I just want to clarify, Your Honour, that military police can only be soldiers and they can't be with MUP as my friend has suggested, but I will use different language if Your Honour would like me to proceed with this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir, do you know what unit this military policeman was attached to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Again, I object. She can ask the question which unit. He can then say if he was a military police or he was MUP. He was dressed in black.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, he's already said he was a military policeman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I think the witness already told us that he's a military policeman. There's no problem about that. You may proceed, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you answer that question, sir? Do you know what unit he was attached to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: No. I didn't know then and I don't know now which unit he was attached to.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Just getting back to what you were telling us earlier, sir, when you were digging the grave, that first grave, did you see Dragan Mirkovic at any point in time at any point during the day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes. He came over on that day, and on the next day. He came over to see me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And did he say anything to you on that day, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: The next day he said that there were dead bodies in Kravica to be dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did he say anything else? Did he tell you what you were supposed to do that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if he said anything else. He only said that and nothing else. Maybe he did say another word or two, but I don't believe so. He said that there was work to be done in Kravica and bodies to be taken away.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And was that before or after the military policeman came to see you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: The police officer came on that second night, but this happened on that second day during the day. So Mirkovic came before.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. All right, sir, I'm going to show you a photograph of a machine and ask you whether you recognise it. Do you recognise that photograph, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes, of course I recognise it. These are machines that I know how to operate; that's my profession. And this is a loader, a ULT-200. The one that we see depicted here was not used but there was one similar to it that was used. It was 160-ULT loader.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And when you're referring to the 160-ULT loader, when was that used? Was that used for the first grave or the second grave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: It was used for loading the bodies from Kravica. It was a ULT-160B. I think it had a B marking, but it doesn't matter. It could be a B or a C. It's just a series model indication.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honour, that was Exhibit P63.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, do you have a photograph of a tipper?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I believe I do, Your Honour, and perhaps I can just show that to the witness at this point.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise this. This is a bulldozer with caterpillar wheels, but the same model depicted here was not used. This type of bucket is not used in assignments like this. The bucket would be facing the other way in this kind of assignment.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. So are you saying that you did not use this type of model in your diggings at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I did use a machine like this to dig the second grave. It's a BGH-900, and it has a very long arm that extends 8 to 10 metres, except the bucket is turned towards the vehicle rather than out -- facing out from the vehicle. So it's a different type of machine.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And for the record, Your Honour, that was Exhibit P62.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, before we go to the details in that incident, could we have a break?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, sir, before we turn to your tasks at Kravica warehouse, going back to when you finished digging the first grave and you said you went home with your machine, can you tell us where did you park your machine precisely?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I said before that I parked it in front of the public utilities company near the petrol station and the fire station. That's where the area is where I parked the machine.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. So then, dealing with your tasks at the Kravica warehouse, you indicated that Dragan Mirkovic, the day before, gave you instructions to go to the Kravica warehouse. Did you meet with Dragan Mirkovic the day that you went to Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Dragan Mirkovic was together with me in the period when I was covering up, burying the bodies, and when we set out for this assignment that morning, he drove in front of me in his own vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what did you do upon arrival to Kravica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: When we came to Kravica, we started loading. I began to load with my small machine. I was working with a mask.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And when you say you began to load, what are you referring to, loading what and from where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I started to load the bodies of dead Muslims who were there in that area, in that building.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And where did you load them, on to what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I loaded them on the trucks which came in the meantime, the same trucks which were there the previous day.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And who was driving those trucks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Cvjetinovic drove those trucks, the yellow truck, Stanojevic drove the red truck, and Ivan drove another truck which kept breaking down. He switched with Simic because Simic was with me with a loader on that assignment. So Ivan drove that truck.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And how long did you -- how much time did you spend loading the bodies from the warehouse on to the trucks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I started loading the bodies, then I felt sick because of the stench. It was seeping through the mask, so I wasn't able to load up the full truck. They took me to one side so that I could recover, because I was feeling very sick because of the stench. I wanted to throw up.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And where did you go when you felt sick?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I was taken back to town to take up some rest. [redacted] [redacted]. When I recovered, they took me back again in the small tipper so that I could start digging the other large grave in Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And who took you back to the town to recover?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I was taken back in some car. I don't know, it was some type of military vehicle. I don't know what kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, do you know who was driving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: No, because I wasn't really quite conscious, so I really don't know who drove the car.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you describe, sir, precisely where you were at the Kravica warehouse, where exactly it's located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: The Kravica warehouse is an agricultural cooperative and it's on the Bratunac/Konjevic Polje road. When you are going from the direction of the Bratunac, it is located on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Turning then to Prosecution Exhibit 10.1, I'm going to ask you if you can identify where you were.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: This is a diagram of the Kravica agricultural cooperative, and this area between the cement walls, that's where it was, that's where my machine was when I started loading. It was at this middle entrance, so to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And are you referring then, sir, to the building on the far right of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's the large building where there's this large open area without doors. That's where the bodies were.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps, Your Honour, given the importance of the evidence I'm going to ask that the photograph be placed on the ELMO and the witness point to it precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you point out, sir, where you were loading the bodies.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: This is the road leading to the building, then you can see four entrances. This is where they used to keep something. I don't know what they used to keep there. That's where the bodies were at this second entrance, that's where I would go in with the machine, then I would back out. There was a truck parked next to the machine and I would load the bodies there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And just for the record the witness is referring to the second entrance from the right of the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You indicated, sir, that you returned to dig the second grave at some point. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And when did you return to dig the second grave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I returned when I had recovered. I had begun to feel better, so I came back. That was in the afternoon. I don't know whether that was at 11.00, 12.00, 12.30, I really don't know. Nobody was looking at the time, least of all me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And how did you know where you were to dig the second grave? How did you know what the location was of the second grave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: When the first grave was being dug, Mirkovic and Nikolic said to start digging the second grave nearby in an area adjacent to it, to the first.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right, sir, I'm going to ask you then to refer to your diagram. Perhaps Mr. Usher can assist us on placing that on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: For the record, that is Prosecution Exhibit P164.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you show us, sir, where you were instructed to dig the second grave, and where you in fact dug the second grave.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: The second grave was dug just opposite from the first one, perhaps a metre or two diagonally from it because there was a small wood there, so it wasn't possible to dig immediately next to the first grave. So it was a few, maybe up to 5 metres, further away that the digging began.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And for the record, Your Honour, the witness is pointing to the right of the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And when you returned, sir, to dig the second grave, what machine did you use?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: The second grave I started digging with the same small machine that I used while digging the first grave.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you use any other machine while you were digging?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: At the time I did not use any other machine, just that one.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you see any other machine located near the location of that grave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: No. There were no other machines located near the graves at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: When you and I met, sir, the other day, I gave you an information report to read over to assist you in refreshing your memory. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps then, sir, I'm going to give you a copy of the information report in your own language and ask you to read it to yourself. I'll be asking you, sir, to read the second paragraph from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes, I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Does that assist you in refreshing your memory as to whether or not there was another machine at that site?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: It states here: "The next day during the night," this is already the night, it's not that day, "an excavator was brought which was used to dig the water pipes, trenches for that. Before that, I was using my small machine to work on the redirection of the flow of the river, so that is -- and this other machine was used for that as well. So that is how I knew about that machine."

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Does that assist -- does that paragraph, sir, assist you if you look at the last line of the paragraph to refresh your memory as to whether or not you used this machine to dig this second grave?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't mean to be picky about this. I suspect everyone has this information report. It was generated as a result of the tape recording not functioning, as I understand it. So if that is the case, first perhaps the witness should be asked if he did indicate this to the investigator at the time when he was being interviewed, if he recalls. And then if the answer is yes, does this refresh his memory, something to that effect. At least we can have some foundational steps laid down, otherwise we would have to have this individual come in here and lay some foundation at some other point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think we have been working with this report for a while and we'll hear what the witness is going to tell us. Of course you have the right to cross-examine this person when your turn is coming.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, sir, have you read that entire paragraph now to yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Does that assist you in refreshing your memory as to what machine you used in digging that second grave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes, it does, because the next day I continued to dig that grave with that same machine.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And what is that -- what machine did you use to dig that grave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I think that it was a loader, a Caterpillar bulldozer or loader, but the bucket is facing the actual body of the vehicle and not facing out from it, like the one that you showed us.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Well, perhaps we can refer to that photograph again just so that we understand what you're telling us.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And I believe it was Exhibit P62.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a similar machine to the one I used, but this bucket does not face outward for loading but it faces towards the cabin, that is the difference between the two machines, and it has a broader, a wider, range and it works faster.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Do you know, sir, where this machine was brought from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I think that this machine was in Bratunac. I said that before. When we were redirecting the flow of a river before these events; this was a river that flooded the school, so we had to redirect the bed, the flow, of the river by about 2 to 300 metres in order to prevent the flooding.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did this machine have any particular markings on it that you noticed that indicates to you where it was from, where it's origin is from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes. I've said before that the water pipes of -- Zvornik, it had a marking on it "Zvornik SO," it's a plate, a licence plate on the vehicle identifying it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what colour was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: It was yellow, just like all the other machinery.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And what was the size of the second grave that you dug?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: It says here that it was about 20 metres long, about 10 to 15 metres wide, and maybe 2 to 3 metres deep, because this is a larger machine, so the bucket has a larger capacity and the arm is longer.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: When you were first given the order, sir, to dig this second grave, were you told why or the reason as to why a second grave was required?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: The reason that was given was that that building which was located at the agricultural cooperative contained bodies of Muslims which needed to be buried in this pit, in this grave.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And when you say "the reason that was given," who gave you that reason? Who told you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Dragan Mirkovic and Momir Nikolic explained this to me. The other Nikolic was also present, the one who was the director of the cooperative.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what's his first name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: It is noted there as Jole.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. I'm actually going to just ask you to put that piece of paper aside, sir. And where were you when Dragan Mirkovic, Momir Nikolic, and Jole Nikolic were present and it was explained to you the reason why a second grave was required?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Where was I?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I was digging the first grave when Mirkovic was telling me that, and then the next day when I started up the loading of the bodies from the cooperative, I was told that again in front of that same building, in front of the second entrance.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And just to clarify, sir, was anybody with Dragan Mirkovic the first day when you were digging the first grave when you were first told to dig a second grave, was there anyone else present besides Dragan Mirkovic that first time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Dragan came once or twice during the course of that day to see how I was doing, to see if the machine was working, and so on, and he was by himself on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And once you started or completed digging the second grave, sir, what happened at that point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: When the digging of the second grave was finished, the trucks from the Kravica cooperative that were waiting there came one by one, brought the bodies, and tipped them into the grave.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And approximately how many bodies were placed into the grave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: The exact number is not known. I don't know it. Nobody was counting, and if the trucks came back two or three times, multiply the number of the bodies that were in the trucks and how many can fit into the grave. You just need to multiply that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. What did you do after the bodies were placed in the pit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: After the bodies were placed in the pit, I gradually, using the machine, the large machine, grabbed the earth from one pile that had been -- of excavated earth and layer by layer was spreading it into the grave.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And when did you do that, sir? When did you cover up the grave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: The grave was covered up only late on the second day. That's when it was completely finished.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Was there anybody present during your process of covering up the grave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I don't believe anyone was present. The stench was too strong and the infection was spreading. I think I was the only person around.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: With respect to both the first and second graves, sir, did you see any military police while you were digging the graves or while you were covering up the graves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: No. I didn't see anyone then, at least where I was. My radius of work was between 5 and 10 metres and I was not exactly looking left and right as I was working.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Were you given any orders to dig other graves after you completed the second grave at Kravica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: There were perhaps several bodies left that were there. When people returned to their homes, they found the bodies and reported this. So the yellow lorry belonging to the public utilities company would bring those bodies on the next day. So these additional bodies were buried next to the first grave, maybe five or six bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And how long after the huge burial operation did you dig these smaller graves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: It was over the next couple of days, perhaps one or two days later. I think the next day, the third, fourth, fifth, or sixth day.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you remember how many bodies were brought to the smaller graves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: As I said, five or six bodies, roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Then referring again to your diagram, sir, P164, if I can ask the usher to assist us, please. Can you indicate, sir, on the diagram where you dug the smaller graves, using the pointer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Here, it was an extension of the first grave, several metres, 2 or 3 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And how many graves did you dig? How many smaller graves did you dig?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Here you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: As I said, five or six graves in a line. It was here, like an extension.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And just for the record, Your Honour, the witness has referred to the right of the first grave that was -- that's been depicted on the photograph or on the diagram.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, how many bodies were brought to these smaller graves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: As I said, five or six bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. I thought you said you were talking about five or six smaller graves. I just want to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Which other ones do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Are you saying you dug five or six smaller graves or there were five or six bodies brought to these smaller graves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Five or six bodies brought to those graves and five or six bodies buried in a line, where the extension of this grave was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, after this period of time, sir, were you asked to participate in the digging or digging up of these same graves at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes. It was requested after a certain time when there was no longer any imminent threat of war and when I alongside with other people started living a normal life, we were back to normal life, Momir Nikolic was requested to have the graves dug up again, to be transferred to a different location for fear of an infection spreading. People were beginning to return to their homes which were near the graves.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And when did this occur, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: As I said, maybe a month or two. It was autumn. I can't remember the exact date. Some people may know the date. Maybe Momir knows the exact date, but when we received this order we protested. The same team was called back. No one was there to assist us, to protect us from this order. We had to do it and that was that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And when you say, sir, the same team was called back, what do you mean by that specifically? Who was that team?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: This same team with the lorries and machines.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And where did you -- where were you when you were given this order by Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: We were outside the wooden shack. He came to pick us up and he gave us this order.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And when you refer, sir, to the wooden shack, is that the same place that you referred to earlier, the military police building? You have to speak into the microphone, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And who was present when Momir Nikolic gave these -- this order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: When Momir gave us this order, present there were the lorry drivers led by the men who were operating the machines.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Was there anyone else present, aside from the lorry drivers and yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I believe Mirkovic was there, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Anybody else, sir, that you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Not that I can recall now, but I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, to assist you in refreshing your memory, sir, I'm going to ask you to refer to your transcript, which is on the table there, and to refer to specifically page 53 in your transcript, lines 20 through 21.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And in the English version, Your Honour, page 74, lines 19 through 21.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You can actually start, sir, with the question at line 18 in your transcript.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes, I've had a look.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Does that assist you in refreshing your memory as to whether or not there was anybody else present, aside from the persons you've mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes. It's stated very clearly here. Momir Nikolic, the men who operated the machines, the lorry drivers, and his escort, his two policemen. He knows who they were; I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And when you say "policemen," sir, what specifically, what type of policemen are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Military policemen who were with him. I don't know who they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Was there another -- any other drivers, sir, aside from the drivers that you've named earlier that were involved in the reburial operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. What did you do once you received these orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Once we had received this order, it was in the afternoon, we were taken to the petrol station to get fuel for the machines and lorries.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you start working that same night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes. That same night we started work.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what did you do specifically? What was the work that you did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I was digging, lifting bodies out of the grave using my equipment. There was another excavator being used, operated by the other colleague who was there working with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And which graves did you lift the bodies out of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: The grave to the left, number one, and grave number two. Those were the graves from which we were lifting bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Those are the graves you were referring to earlier at Glogova. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, in Glogova. Yes, those were the graves.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And can you describe the machine you were using to lift the bodies out of the graves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I can describe the machine. It's very much like the one in your sketch, except that the type is 160B or C, which doesn't really make any difference. It's a loader belonging to the brickworks.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Were the same trucks used for the reburial operation that were used in the initial burial at Glogova?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes, the same lorries.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you know where the bodies were taken to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: The bodies travelled down that street. I wish you could have been there to see for yourself, because you could hardly see in the dark where they were taking the bodies, could you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay, sir, we're just trying to understand what happened. Can you tell us when you say the bodies travelled down that street, what street are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: They came out of that street and came on to the main road to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps it might help you, sir, to refer to your diagram to show us what street. Would that assist you? Okay, if we can then refer to Prosecution Exhibit 164, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: We were lifting bodies from this first grave. They took this small street and then got on to the main road for Bratunac passing through Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So you're indicating, sir, that the bodies went to the direction of Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes. It was dark. The lorries started out, took this road towards Bratunac. They came out onto the main road to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. During the course of the reburial operation, sir, did you notice whether or not there were any military police present at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: It was dark. I couldn't notice anyone around me in my surroundings from where I was sitting inside the machine, with the exception of my colleague who was there operating his own machine.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And just by way of clean-up, Your Honour, I just have a couple more questions to go back to. Sir, can you tell us when you -- just going back to the initial grave, the grave number two, at Kravica, when you said you were sick and you went home and you returned back to Glogova to dig that second grave, how did you get back to Glogova?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: As I said, I was driven there in a car. I was driven to Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you know who drove you back to Glogova?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I think it was the lorries, this colleague who came to pick me up.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And who is this colleague, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: The one who worked with me in the public utilities company, Cvjetinovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And, sir, when you initially returned the machine to the town, to the public utilities company, after you completed digging the first grave at Glogova, did you clean the machine at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: We didn't have the equipment we needed to clean the machine. Some of the earth came off the bucket by itself, but we couldn't clean anything that was still left there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you clean the machine, sir, after you completed the digging of the second grave at Glogova?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I don't think the machine was cleaned even then. Perhaps later, once the excavation and secondary excavation had been done and the machines had been washed from the smell of dead bodies, because the stench had penetrated the cabin and all other parts of the machine.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can just have the Court's indulgence for a moment, please. Sorry, Your Honour, I do just have one more area that I'd like to explore.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, how did you react when you received the order to dig up the bodies from the graves in the fall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: We all had the same reaction: Why us? Why us again receiving the same kind of orders as before? However, there was nothing you could do about it. They just told us, you, the same team who had done the digging the last time around, you should do it again. We did try to speak out against this, we did try to make a stand, but it was to no avail.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you feel you had a choice in the matter at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: How am I supposed to know whether I had a choice? That certainly wasn't my impression. Our pleas were no use. Our pleas did not help us to avoid this fate.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did anything happen, sir, before -- just before you were given the order to cause you to feel you didn't have a choice in the matter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Well, there were invitations -- or rather, calls that I talked about the investigator in Banja Luka. There were threats, all kinds of things, and we just sort of put two and two together in our heads. We saw that the situation was like that and we simply had to get the job done.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. So when you say there were threats, there were calls, can you clarify that. When did these calls occur?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: That autumn before the bodies were moved -- you know what telephones are like, how on earth was I to know who the caller was, but there were threats to the safety of my family. Those were threats. That's what it was and that's how we saw the situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: What made you think that the threats were related to the reburial operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I don't know why we felt that way, but we put two and two together.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Cross-examination. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, although I don't know if I'll be able to finish with the amount of time that we have, but I can begin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, just start normally to see how far you go.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And if I could move over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I want to pick up just in the area where you left off, dealing with the reburials. As I understand it, when you were asked to perform that task, you had indicated that you were back to your normal life. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And by that, should I also assume that you were back to doing your civilian work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes, civilian work, because the infrastructure for civilians had been completely destroyed, the telephone lines and all those of things, and I would go up and down with the tipper truck. They were repairing the water pipes, the phone lines, to get the infrastructure of civilian life in Srebrenica up and running at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And who were you working for at that time in your civilian life?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: My civilian life, I was again with the public utilities unit, and I went to the public utilities established in Srebrenica to repair the water pipes as well as PTT that had been set up in Srebrenica. You had to get the phone lines working again, because they had been destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And who was your supervisor at that point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Dragan Mirkovic was also with the public utilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The same Dragan Nikolic that you have been referring to all day that morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Mirkovic, Dragan Mirkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mirkovic. Thank you. So if I understand you correctly, you're not with the Bratunac Brigade Workers' Battalion when they come back to you and they say, you have to go back and do some reburials. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I was no longer with the Workers' Battalion when the first grave was being dug up, and then the second one. I was no longer with the Workers' Battalion, I was only part of the public utilities unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. We're going to talk about the first one later on, because we have those dates that you've indicated. But I just want to focus now on the reburial aspect. As I understand it, prior to getting that assignment, your family began receiving some threatening calls. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Others were, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Others were, too. And it was made clear that the safety of your wife and your children was at risk if you did not go ahead and carry out the orders that you were about to receive. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: That's correct, yes. That's how I thought it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And we're trying to make a record, so you have to answer -- as opposed to just shaking your head to make sure. So here you were in civilian life when Momir Nikolic comes to you and gives you the order. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I assume that since you had these threats that perhaps Momir Nikolic was the one behind those threats to you and your loved ones.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I don't know who was behind those threats.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But Momir Nikolic was the one that came to you and told you that you had no choice but to perform those duties. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you protested?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: That's correct, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You and the others told Momir Nikolic that you did not want to participate in this activity. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And Momir Nikolic told you you had no choice.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I think that's precisely what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, you knew you had no choice because you had been receiving threats, you and your family had been receiving threats what would happen to your family if you refused the order which ultimately came from Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: That was our idea of the whole situation, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And Momir Nikolic was still in the army, was he not? He was still in service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you were not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I was back to civilian life with the public utilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, was the public utilities also part of the civil protection unit? Were they involved in civil protection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes, it was part of the civilian protection, taking part in the asanacija of the terrain, repairing phone lines and everything else in the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that's part of the civilian authority, is it not, not the military authority?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes, it was part of the civilian authority, and it still is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Correct. And it's part of the -- the civil authority is responsible for what is commonly known as asanacija?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Probably so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you had been familiar with that type of work, even prior to July 1995. Isn't that right? Before July 1995, you had been familiar with asanacija, the work performed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes, I was in the asanacija unit of the civilian protection and the public utilities company, so I was familiar with that work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And that was part of your contribution to the war effort. Rather than being a soldier on the front, you were part of the civil protection unit performing the task of asanacija when necessary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then there came a time when you were also called upon to be a member of the Workers' Battalion. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact we have the paperwork that you've shown us, that there was a period of time when you were officially called on and signed in to be performing your duties in the Workers' Battalion. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I have that document and the Prosecution also has it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And the Workers' Battalion wasn't in charge of or responsible for asanacija, was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I think that the Workers' Battalion at the time was just on the line. It wasn't responsible for asanacija, just the same as me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And when you -- I'm having a hard time hearing the translator. When you were on the front line, you were performing duties similar to any other combat soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You're sitting there, waiting for something to happen, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes. And if I'm caught by a bullet, who would be responsible? Nobody.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And there you were sitting on the front line waiting for something to happen when all of a sudden Srebrenica falls. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know exactly who it was that gave that message to pass on to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I don't know who gave the message, but the messenger had found us in the woods where we were on the line that day and the commander, Nedjo Mladjenovic, told Djurkovic to go back along the line, back to town, because you're needed in town for asanacija.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So he merely passed on --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, if we could just take a break for a minute. It might be helpful just to resolve some issues that we have related to some exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I find this rather unusual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, unless you give me the sufficient reasons for that, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I just want to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I think I get the gist of it. I get the gist of it. My colleague --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I can withdraw it, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey is absolutely correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I'm doing some make-up work right now, but you have to be very cautious.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour, and I must apologise because I'm a little tired and not familiar with -- not used to going in and out, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So you received a call to go back to town. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, do you know exactly who it was that passed on the message, who requested you to come to town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: I don't know who it was exactly, but I only got the message from Commander Nedjo to return to town.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And Komandir Nedjo, he was merely passing on a message to you. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: Yes, he was just passing the message on via a radio station, Motorola.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. In other words, he wasn't ordering you, he wasn't giving you an order on behalf of the Workers' Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade, but area he was transmitting a message to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140
utterances.text: [redacted] [redacted] You are requested or you are needed for the asanacija of the terrain and this is what I was told and that's what I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wonder if we could go into private session just very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, let's go into the private session. I think this is the safest way to conduct the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in the open session. Witness, I'm sorry to say that we did not finish your testimony today and you have to stay in The Hague for three days more. And during that period, I want to know -- I want you to know that you are still under the oath, so do not talk to anybody about your testimony and do not let anybody talk to you about your testimony. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will resume on Monday morning at 9.00 in the same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
